sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds is an elected county office that keeps Carbon County's land records, from deeds and mortgages to easements and rights of way. When a house sells in Jim Thorpe, Lehighton, Palmerton or any other Carbon County town, the deed has to be recorded here before the public record shows the new owner.

Every document goes through three steps: indexing into the public retrieval system, scanning, and a check of the index entries. One copy sits on the county's public system, Landex, and two archive copies are kept on secure servers at separate locations. The office also collects realty transfer tax and the court-related fees that go to the state, plus the Affordable Housing Program fee that supports income-based housing in the county.

A deed or mortgage costs $102.75 under the fee sheet effective November 17, 2025. That covers four pages, four names and one parcel number.

Carbon County recording fees, effective November 17, 2025
DocumentRecording fee
Deed$102.75
Mortgage$102.75
Assignment, release or satisfaction of mortgage$74.75
Agreement of sale$74.75
Easement or right of way$74.75
Mortgage modification or subordination$33.50
Power of attorney$18.50

Longer documents cost more. Deeds and mortgages add $4.00 for each page past four, other documents add $2.00 per page past four, every name beyond four adds $0.50, and each extra parcel number adds $15.00. Pay the exact amount in cash, personal check, business check or money order. A wrong amount comes back with a $5.00 rejection fee, though the county keeps an overpayment of $10.00 or less.

The office collects 2% of the total consideration or the fair market value, and the money is divided among the state, local school districts and municipalities. A Pennsylvania Statement of Value, form REV-183, is required whenever you aren't paying tax on full market value.

  • All trusts require a Statement of Value.
  • Easements need one unless the grantee is a public utility.
  • A transfer out of an estate needs one unless full tax is being paid.
  • Submit the form in duplicate. Its pages don't count toward the page total.
  • A family transfer, such as a parent to children, must be typed on the deed if no tax is being paid.

Use the Common Level Ratio factor for the year your document is dated. For factors older than five years, call the office at 570-325-2651.

sections.h2: Where to file and the daily cutoff
sections.html:
Carbon County takes recordings by mail, in person and through the e-recording partners CSC and Simplifile. The office number is 570-325-2651. Recording closes at 3:30 p.m., so a closing that wraps up late in the day may not record until the next business day.

Documents must relate to real estate, be in English or carry a translation, and bear original, properly notarized signatures. A mailed filing needs a self-addressed stamped envelope, and a holder of an office mailbox is asked to pick up recorded papers at least weekly. Remote online notarization is accepted when the certificate says the notarial act used communication technology.

The county's recording requirements run to 21 items, and the same few mistakes come up again and again.

  • The document date must match or precede the acknowledgment date.
  • Grantor names, signatures and acknowledgments must match exactly, and the names should match the prior deed's grantee.
  • Reference documents must show the book and page of the earlier recorded paper.
  • State the municipality, whether township or borough, above the legal description. For land in several localities, show the percentage split for local transfer tax on the Statement of Value.
  • Deeds, mortgages, easements, releases and assignments need a signed mailing address certification, because that address tells the Assessment Office where to send property tax bills.
  • Notary blocks need the right venue, a legible stamp and a current commission expiration date.

Records are published through Landex. Landex Webstore gives the public remote access to documents from 1988 forward, and a separate Landex Remote service serves title searchers. Anyone can sign up for a Landex Record Alert on a name or a tax parcel number and get a notice whenever a new document is recorded against it.

An alert is a cheap way for a seller to confirm that a satisfaction of mortgage was recorded after payoff, or for an heir to watch for filings against an inherited house. Staff can also help trace a property back through earlier owners and purchase prices, and help replace a lost document.

  • A re-recorded document needs a new acknowledgment and new signatures.
  • When several documents are filed together, label them, such as POA, deed and mortgage, so they record in the right order.
  • Sales agreements must list the full address of both buyer and seller.

sections.h2: Releases and satisfactions before you sell
sections.html:
If you have a mortgage, the lender's satisfaction has to be recorded so the title is clear for the next owner. A satisfaction applies when the whole loan is paid off. A release, sometimes called a partial release, applies when part of the property or one name comes off the mortgage while the loan stays active on the rest.

Each satisfaction or release can reference only one mortgage, and blanket documents are refused. Trust transfers have their own rule. Since October 1, 2024, deeds into a trust can't be e-recorded, so they must be brought in or mailed. For tax parcel numbers on agreements, easements, leases and rights of way, call the county GIS department at 570-325-8519 first.

Run through a short list. Confirm the grantor and grantee names match the prior deed, and that the acknowledgment date is the same or later than the document date. Get your parcel number from the Assessment Office at 570-325-5254. Count pages and parcels so you can send the exact fee, since a wrong amount means a rejection fee and a delay. If the closing is late in the day, file electronically through CSC or Simplifile so it is in before 3:30 p.m., unless the deed goes into a trust, which must come by hand or mail.

Carbon County was split off from Northampton County in 1843. Jim Thorpe is the seat and Palmerton is the largest borough. I-80 and the Northeast Extension of the Pennsylvania Turnpike (I-476) cross the county. It has 65,868 residents in 2025 on about 381 square miles, with 34,816 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median home value was $211,400, owner-occupancy was 76.4% and median gross rent was $994. About 24.3% of residents are 65 or older.

faqs.q: What time does the Carbon County Recorder of Deeds stop recording?
faqs.a: The cutoff for recording is 3:30 p.m. Documents arriving after that time wait for the next business day, so plan closings with that in mind.

faqs.q: How much is the realty transfer tax in Carbon County?
faqs.a: The office collects 2% of the total consideration or the fair market value of the property. That money is distributed to the state, the local school district and the municipality.

faqs.q: Can a deed into a trust be e-recorded in Carbon County?
faqs.a: No. Since October 1, 2024, the office accepts deeds into a trust only in person or by mail. Other documents can still be e-recorded through CSC or Simplifile.

faqs.q: Do I need a UPI to record a Carbon County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. All real estate documents need a Uniform Parcel Identifier before recording. Call the Assessment Office at 570-325-5254 to get one, and add $15.00 for each parcel beyond the first.

faqs.q: What happens if I pay the wrong recording fee in Carbon County?
faqs.a: The document is returned and a $5.00 rejection fee is charged per document. The one exception is an overpayment of $10.00 or less, which the county keeps.
